public_rationale: Primary documentation shows a conspicuous English imbalance on both sides of the claim. InstructGPT's instruction data was overwhelmingly English, BIG-G's training mixture contained little non-English text, and HELM's initial core evaluations covered only English. BIG-bench also acknowledged limited lower-resource coverage. BLOOM and xP3 are important multilingual exceptions, so the supported reading is broad predominance rather than a universal English-only rule.
limitations: The assessment concerns language systems in the post's context, not all AI applications.
Instruction tuning, pretraining, and evaluation coverage measure different aspects of the imbalance.
No exact industry-wide English share or universal performance gap is established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI systems and AI test sets have a huge English-language bias.

statement.excerpt: AI and AI test sets have a huge English-language bias.

from_speaker: DO run tests in other languages
our_interpretation: In context, AI refers to GPT-like language systems and their language and reasoning evaluations, not every kind of artificial intelligence.

The plain reading is substantial English predominance in model development and evaluation coverage, with weaker representation of other languages. It does not assert that every model or benchmark is English-only.
Huge describes a conspicuous imbalance; no numerical cutoff or population-weighting formula is supplied.
For this ongoing research-state observation, use the latest completed research year and the elapsed publication year: 2022 through 17 February 2023. This observation window is evaluator-selected.
criteria.support_condition: Primary documentation shows substantial English predominance in the training or tuning of prominent contemporary language models and in major general-purpose evaluation suites.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative documentation shows broadly balanced language coverage in both contemporary language-model development and major evaluation suites, without substantial English predominance.

evidence.locator: Section 5, limitations of data collection; Appendix A.4
evidence.explanation: The developer reports that roughly 96% of its instruction dataset was classified as English, possibly more because of classifier errors. This directly supports English predominance in instruction tuning, without treating that percentage as the pretraining distribution.

evidence.locator: Section 3.1, Languages; introduction's description of the 16 core scenarios
evidence.publisher: Liang et al., Stanford CRFM, arXiv
evidence.explanation: HELM's initial core scenarios covered only English, including different English varieties. The authors explicitly say that even multilingual BLOOM was evaluated only for English.

evidence.excerpt: a handful also target lower-resource languages
evidence.publisher: Srivastava et al., BIG-bench collaboration, arXiv
evidence.explanation: BIG-bench documents limited lower-resource-language coverage and reports that its BIG-G training mixture contained about 6% non-English text. Its multilingual tasks also show that English predominance coexisted with deliberate efforts to test other languages.

BLOOM was trained on 46 natural languages, and the project developed a multilingual prompted dataset collection. These are substantial exceptions to an English-only description, but do not negate predominance in other prominent systems and evaluations.
